lessons.title: Welcome to UCA
lessons.content:
Welcome to another part of your UCA journey.

Whether you're here to become a better Graphic Designer, Video Editor, Content Writer, or Communication & Influence specialist, you're not only here to learn a skill.

One of the core foundations of UCA is learning how to build and own your personal brand.

The world is changing quickly. Skills matter, but simply having a skill is no longer enough. People need to know who you are, what you do, what you stand for, and what you can create.

That is why every UCA participant is expected to build a personal brand account during the academy.

For UCA, Instagram is your primary personal-brand platform.

Regardless of the pathway you're studying, your Instagram account will serve as your main public identity and a place where you can begin documenting your journey, showcasing your work, connecting with people, and building an audience.

You may also create one additional platform based on your pathway and goals.

For example, a Content Writing participant may choose a platform such as Substack to publish longer-form writing and build a body of written work.

Your additional platform should complement your Instagram account—not replace it.

lessons.title: Your UCA Personal Brand Goal
lessons.content:
Your Instagram account is not being created simply because UCA requires you to have one.

You are building an actual public presence.

Throughout the 90-day UCA sprint, 500 Instagram followers is the minimum benchmark for graduation.

That number is the floor, not the ceiling.

The goal is not to chase followers for the sake of having a number. The goal is to learn how to build an audience around your skills, perspective, personality, work, and journey.

If you take the process seriously, 500 should be a starting point—not the end goal.

lessons.title: Today's Focus
lessons.content:
Today, you will establish the foundation of your personal brand account.

You will:

- Create your Instagram account
- Choose your username
- Set up your profile
- Select an appropriate profile picture
- Complete your basic account information
- Optimise your profile for the person you want to become
- Understand how your profile should represent your pathway and personal brand

You do not need to become an Instagram expert today.

The goal is simply to build a strong foundation that you can develop throughout the academy.

lessons.title: Getting Started on Instagram
lessons.content:
If you do not already have an Instagram account dedicated to your personal brand, create one today.

If you already have an account you intend to use for your personal brand, you do not necessarily need to create another one. Instead, you can begin optimising the account you already have.

Your account should make it clear that there is a real person behind it and that person is becoming increasingly skilled at something.

Your pathway should influence the direction of your account.

For example:

Graphic Design:
Your profile should eventually communicate that you are a designer and give people a reason to explore your work.

Video Editing:
Your profile should communicate that you are an editor and eventually become a place where your edits, projects, experiments, and creative journey can be seen.

Content Writing:
Your Instagram can become the front door to your personal brand, while an additional writing platform can serve as a deeper home for your writing.

Communication & Influence:
Your content can demonstrate your ideas, communication ability, perspective, and understanding of people.

You are not expected to have everything figured out today.

You are establishing the foundation.

lessons.title: Optimise Your Profile
lessons.content:
Once your account has been created, the next step is making sure your profile represents you properly.

Your Instagram profile is often the first thing someone sees before deciding whether to follow you.

That means every important element of your profile should work together.

Pay attention to:

- Username
- Name field
- Profile picture
- Bio
- Keywords
- Category
- Link
- Contact information
- Highlights
- Pinned content

You don't need to master every one of these elements today.

The important thing is to understand why your profile needs to be intentional.

Your username should be recognisable.

Your profile picture should make you identifiable and present you appropriately.

Your name field and bio should help people understand who you are and what you do.

Your keywords should make your area of interest or expertise easier to understand.

Your category should accurately represent your account where appropriate.

Your links and contact information should make it easy for people to take the next step when necessary.

Your highlights and pinned content should eventually help a new visitor understand your work, personality, journey, or most important content.

A BRIEF OVERVIEW

Watch the lesson below, then take notes. Don't simply copy what the tutorial does — understand the principles behind the optimisation and think about how they apply to your own personal brand.

lessons.title: Think Beyond Instagram
lessons.content:
Instagram is the primary personal-brand platform for UCA, but the principles you're learning today are not exclusive to Instagram.

The same thinking applies to other platforms.

Your LinkedIn profile, X profile, TikTok profile, YouTube channel, Substack, portfolio, or any other platform you eventually use should communicate a consistent identity.

The platform may change.

The format may change.

The audience may change.

But the foundation remains:

Who are you?
What do you do?
What do you want to be known for?
Why should someone care?

Learn the principle, then adapt it to the platform.

lessons.title: Today's Task
lessons.content:
By the end of today's session, you should have:

☐ Created or selected your personal-brand Instagram account
☐ Set an appropriate username
☐ Added an appropriate profile picture
☐ Completed your basic profile information
☐ Written an initial bio that reflects your direction
☐ Selected an appropriate category
☐ Added relevant contact information where necessary
☐ Set up your profile with your UCA pathway in mind
☐ Identified an additional platform you may use based on your pathway and goals

Remember

Your account does not need to be perfect today.

It needs to exist, be intentional, and be ready to grow.

You will continue developing your personal brand throughout the UCA 90-day sprint.

Today, you're simply putting the foundation in place.

lessons.title: Today's Goal
lessons.content:
Create the account.

Optimise the foundation.

Make your direction clear.

You are not just creating an Instagram account.

You are beginning to build a public identity around who you are, what you can do, and what you are becoming.

lessons.title: Tuesday — Introduction to Personal Branding
lessons.content:
Welcome back.

Yesterday, you created and began setting up your personal brand account.

Today, we take the next step: understanding what you are actually building.

Having an Instagram account is only the beginning.

The goal is to turn that account into a place where people can gradually understand who you are, what you do, what you care about, and what you can offer.

That is where personal branding comes in.

You do not need to become a personal-branding expert today.

You simply need enough clarity to begin creating, posting, and developing your identity in public.

lessons.title: What You'll Learn Today — Personal Branding
lessons.content:
Today, you will build a basic understanding of:

- What personal branding means
- Why personal branding matters
- Who you are trying to communicate with
- Your target audience
- What you want to be known for
- Your area of interest or expertise
- The types of content you can create
- Why consistency matters

These ideas are connected, so rather than treating them as separate lessons, you will learn them in two parts.

lessons.title: Part 1 — Understanding Your Personal Brand
lessons.content:
Personal branding is essentially about how you intentionally present yourself to the world and what people come to associate with you.

It is not simply about having followers.

It is not pretending to be someone you're not.

And it is not trying to make yourself look perfect online.

Your personal brand develops from the combination of your identity, interests, skills, perspective, experiences, work, and the way you consistently communicate them.

Before you start creating content, you need some basic clarity about yourself.

Ask yourself:

What am I interested in?

What am I learning or becoming good at?

What do I want people to associate with me?

What can I talk about or create content around?

You don't need perfect answers.

Your personal brand will evolve as you learn, experiment, and discover more about yourself.

The important thing is to have a direction.

A BRIEF OVERVIEW

Watch the lesson below to understand the foundations of personal branding, why it matters, and how to begin thinking about your own personal brand.

As you watch, think about how the ideas apply specifically to you and your UCA pathway.

lessons.title: Part 2 — Your Audience, Content & Consistency
lessons.content:
Knowing yourself is only one side of personal branding.

You also need to understand who you are communicating with.

Your content should eventually connect with a particular group of people.

This does not mean you need to know your exact audience immediately.

Start by thinking about:

Who would be interested in what I know, create, or have to say?

Who could benefit from my content?

What problems, interests, questions, or aspirations do these people have?

Your answers will help you begin identifying your target audience.

From there, you can start thinking about the type of content you can create.

As a UCA participant, your content can naturally develop around your skill, interests, learning process, experiences, opinions, projects, and perspective.

A Graphic Designer can document designs, share design thoughts, show projects, or teach what they are learning.

A Video Editor can showcase edits, document their progress, share editing insights, or break down their creative process.

A Content Writer can publish written ideas, observations, stories, lessons, and longer-form pieces on an additional writing platform.

A Communication & Influence participant can explore ideas around communication, people, relationships, leadership, and influence.

You don't need to figure out your entire content strategy today.

You simply need enough clarity to start.

And once you start, consistency becomes important.

Your personal brand is not built from one post.

It is built through repeated exposure.

People need to see you, understand you, and associate you with something over time.

Consistency gives your audience the opportunity to recognise you and your work.

A BRIEF OVERVIEW

Watch the lesson below to understand target audiences, content creation, and the role consistency plays in building a personal brand.

As you watch, begin thinking about the type of person you want your content to reach and the kind of content you can realistically create.

lessons.title: Tuesday's Task
lessons.content:
Now it is time to move from understanding to action.

Your personal brand account should already have been created and set up from yesterday.

If you have not created your account yet, stop here and create it before continuing.

You cannot properly progress through this part of the course without having your personal-brand account ready.

Once your account is ready:

☐ Identify what you are interested in or want to be known for
☐ Identify the people you would like your content to reach
☐ Write down 3–5 topics you could create content around
☐ Think about how your UCA pathway can influence your content
☐ Create your first piece of content
☐ Publish it on your personal brand account

Don't wait until everything is perfect.

Start. Learn. Improve. Repeat.

Your personal brand will become clearer through the process of actually creating.

lessons.title: Tuesday's Goal
lessons.content:
Today's goal is not to become a personal-branding expert.

It is to gain enough clarity to start.

By the end of today, you should:

- Understand the basic idea of personal branding
- Know what you want your account to begin representing
- Have a basic idea of who you want to communicate with
- Have some initial content directions
- Understand why consistency matters
- Have your personal brand account ready
- Begin actively posting

Your account is no longer just a profile.

It is the beginning of your public presence.

From today onward, you are no longer waiting to become ready.

You are going to learn by creating.
